label: power into a load: the peak inside the range (bound by certificate)
ask: A 5 V source behind an 11 ohm 1% resistor feeds any load from 1 to 100 ohm. Can the load ever get more than 0.6 W?

rows.name: V
rows.means: the problem states a 5 V source

rows.name: Rs_nom
rows.means: the problem states an 11 ohm resistor

rows.name: tol
rows.means: the problem states 1% tolerance

rows.name: Rs_min
rows.means: minimum source resistance = Rs_nom * (1 - tol) = 11 * 0.99 = 10.89 ohm

rows.name: Rs_max
rows.means: maximum source resistance = Rs_nom * (1 + tol) = 11 * 1.01 = 11.11 ohm

rows.name: RL_min
rows.means: the problem states load from 1 ohm

rows.name: RL_max
rows.means: the problem states load up to 100 ohm

rows.name: P_max
rows.means: maximum power delivered to load over all allowed Rs and RL: for a given Rs, power is maximized when RL = Rs (matched load) provided Rs lies in [RL_min, RL_max]; here Rs_min=10.89 and Rs_max=11.11 are within [1,100], so maximum occurs at RL=Rs. The power at match is V^2/(4*Rs), which decreases as Rs increases. Therefore the overall maximum is at Rs_min: P_max = V^2/(4*Rs_min) = 25/(4*10.89) = 0.5739 W

rows.name: limit
rows.means: the threshold 0.6 W from the question
